text: I have called Norwalk home for 40 years, since buying my first house at age 22. My wife Natalie and I have raised our two children, Christina and Joseph, here. We now enjoy watching our grandson grow up in our community, our home.

Following the example set by my parents, I have spent my life giving back to Norwalk. I served on the Norwalk-La Mirada School Board from 1999 to 2008, including as President, where I helped raise graduation standards and expand educational opportunities. I currently chair the Public Safety Commission and serve on the Social Service Commission. I am a past President of the Norwalk Chamber of Commerce and currently serve on the SELACO Workforce Development Board, connecting residents to good jobs.
As an Area Manager, I am responsible for a multi-million-dollar sales budget, working directly with city officials, public safety leaders, and community organizations.
If elected, I will prioritize public safety, smart development that keeps Norwalk families here, real support for local businesses and jobs, and responsible spending of your tax dollars.
Please vote Richard LeGaspi for Norwalk City Council.
Visit www.RichardLeGaspi.com for more information.

text: Age: 26
Occupation: Environmental Advocate

Daniel Moreno is a lifelong Norwalk resident from a family of immigrants who instilled in him the values of compassion and honesty. As a community organizer, he has a deep understanding of ecological design and community engagement.

He is a proud product of NLMUSD K-12 schools. Daniel attended Norwalk High School before earning his B.S. in Landscape Architecture from California Polytechnic University, Pomona (CPP) as a first-generation college student. While at CPP, Daniel was actively involved in the American Society of Landscape Architects student chapter and served on their board as President and Social Promotions Chair, helping grow student networks with professionals in Southern California and hosting workshops for STEAM school students to learn about landscape architecture. Daniel also volunteers with Norwalk Unides, a local nonprofit organization, co-leading its environmental portfolio of work, including educating residents on native plants and advocating for greater park access and ecologically beneficial urban forests.

As a Norwalk City Council Member, Daniel will continue to focus on improving public services that address affordability and reflect working-class families' needs, while increasing transparency in city government.

text: Age: 64
Occupation: Retired Teacher

I have been happily married to my wife Corrine for 31 years. We are proud parents of two daughters, and grandparents to our grandson. I graduated from Excelsior High, hold a BA in Economics (CSU, Long Beach) and a MS in Educational Administration (CSU, Fullerton). I recently retired in 2024 after 30 years as a high school educator, serving primarily in the Norwalk La Mirada USD. I had the honor of serving as a NLMUSD School Board Member (l995-2004) and a Norwalk City Council Member (2011-2020). Now, as Norwalk navigates critical new developments and economic shifts, I am stepping forward to bring proven, trusted leadership to City Hall.

A city council member's primary responsibility is to hold the city manager accountable to implement the council's policy decisions. My policy priorities for Norwalk include: enhancing safety, being prudent with your tax dollars, maintaining quality city services, improving communication, and creating the conditions for economic prosperity.

Effective leadership requires standing for your values, listening to every perspective, and always doing what is best for the city. I will always be prepared, treat you with respect, and never take you for granted.
I respectfully ask for your vote.

Leonard Shryock

text: As a 20-year resident and middle-school teacher, I am running for City Council for the City of Norwalk to ensure our local government listens first, collaborates, and acts in the best interest of our residents through strength and accountability.
We need responsible, transparent leadership to address our pressing challenges. My priorities include:
Support first responders in the tackling of property crime.
Fix aging streets, sidewalks, and potholes, improve lighting, and expand transportation options.
Ensure wise use of taxpayer dollars and increase spending transparency.
Support responsible housing that fits the city's character, protects neighborhoods, and meets state mandates.
Pursue compassionate, practical solutions connecting individuals with services while keeping public spaces clean and safe.
Expand after-school programs, scholarships, and college-preparatory partnerships.
Protect and expand programs keeping seniors active and connected.
Encourage local investment to help small businesses thrive.
Invest in parks, recreation, community events, and beautification to make this a better place to raise a family.
I humbly ask for your vote on November 3, 2026.
